author_text: Clement of Rome (by tradition; the letter itself speaks for the church at Rome)
context: Written from the church at Rome to the church at Corinth after younger members there deposed the presbyters; uses the phoenix as an image of the resurrection
themes: Church order | Humility | Repentance | Peace | Resurrection
pd_translation: J. B. Lightfoot (1891) | Roberts and Donaldson, Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1 (1885)

author_text: Unknown; written in the voice of Aristeas, a courtier of Ptolemy II Philadelphus (FIG-0010)
date_text: 3rd–2nd century BCE (scholarly range; set in the reign of Ptolemy II)
context: Tells how Ptolemy II Philadelphus (FIG-0010) sent to Jerusalem for seventy-two elders who translated the Jewish Law into Greek at Alexandria — the tradition behind the name Septuagint, not established fact
pd_translation: H. T. Andrews, in R. H. Charles (ed.), The Apocrypha and Pseudepigrapha of the Old Testament (1913) | H. St J. Thackeray (1904)
